title: Willie Woods, a schoolmate pianist who needed sheet music
summary: Willie Woods played only from copies, later became an x-ray technician in Detroit and never played in bands.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, I want to go back a little bit to Pensacola and I wanted to ask you about some people that you might have heard playing there. Did you know a piano player by the name of Willie Woods?
Yeah, she was from me at school together.
He did? What kind of piano did she play? What style?

The only way she played, she had to put them piano copies up there. You couldn't play without it. So what she used to do, she used to go and buy them and I'd give them money to buy them. And she'd come back to them and she said, I ain't going to playin' it over. And then I'd catch them and go to play it. That's the way we used to work together. She died in Detroit. Oh she did? Yeah. She used to come see me. She got to be an x-ray technician there. Oh really? She didn't play piano after she got home?

She just, you know, she'd come to my house and sit down and try to play piano with me, but she always wanted me to play. Because I always had a piano there in Detroit. Did she ever play with bands, do you know? No, I ain't never really played with no bands. Even in Pensacola she played in a band.
You know, played for a soft, you know, like that. She never played with no band like I did.
